What happens when you use the podcast to teach the students the four basic tenses?
Students will write description where they are creating the story themselves, as opposed to recreating the poster images. There is less focus on reproducing the past or the present:
We take the students out of the passive position of just completing a vocabulary task and put them in the position of having to create the story. We ask the students to go beyond the sentences they have been given in the podcast and, using the remember key, create a comic strip in their Post-it Notes.
After the break, we will give them a piece of paper which will then be stuck on. If somebody has forgotten to use the remember key, this is a reminder that they need to use the answer key to see if they have remembered to include everything. There is an element of deliberate revealing for the students at this stage.
They have a very simple assessment where they are evaluated on the quality of their presentation.
Why should we be using comic strips for assessing?
Presentation matters. When you teach, we are often very happy when our students are merely able to communicate. Let's be generous and grade the sentences 4 because they are conveying an idea. But let's be less generous and give the student a lower mark because the quality of her re-creation is not appropriate for a North American culture. By asking them to re-create the story in our culture, we are asking students to interact with North American culture. We are not looking for a rewrite of the poster they saw, we are looking for the story to be recreated in our context.
Comic strips allow the teacher to assess the students on the aspects of their talk and not of their illustrations, and some of the assessments on the comic strips which are done in the classroom focus on the quality of the drawing. I think quality of the drawings can be very useful, but for me assessment focuses on what that student has accomplished when they have asked to evaluate.
When we create a poster, there is a real sense of ownership. It is uploaded to the wall, but also saved and exists as an image online. They can take it home and share with their class members. When they present it to a group of students, they are always very proud of what they have done.
